Let $Q$ be a finite aspherical Poincar\'e complex of formal dimension $n\ge3$, with any orientation character $w$. Then \[ \bt{1}(\widetilde Q)=\bt{n-1}(\widetilde Q)=0 . \] Moreover $\bt{0}(\widetilde Q)=\bt{n}(\widetilde Q)=0$ and $\bt{p}(\widetilde Q)=0$ for $p>n$. The same holds for every closed connected aspherical topological manifold of dimension $n\ge3$.

statement: OpenAI \cite{O}, Sections 3--10: Let $\Gam$ be a finitely presented torsion-free group. Suppose that $\Gam$ has one end, that $H^2(\Gam;\F_2\Gam)=0$, and that $\Gam$ has no splitting over a finite or two-ended subgroup. Then $\bt{1}(\Gam)=0$.
If $n\ge1$, the group $\Gam$ is finitely presented, torsion-free and infinite.

For every left $k\Gam$-module $V$ and every $i$ there is an isomorphism $H^i(\Gam;V)\cong H_{n-i}(\Gam;V)$. For every subgroup $J$ of $\Gam$ and every $i$, \[ H^i(\Gam;k[\Gam/J])\cong H_{n-i}(J;k), \] where $k[\Gam/J]$ is the permutation module with basis the left cosets of $J$.
If $n\ge3$, then $H^1(\Gam;k\Gam)=0$ and $H^2(\Gam;k\Gam)=0$, and $H^1(\Gam;k[\Gam/J])=0$ when $J$ is trivial or infinite cyclic.
An infinite finitely generated group $\Gam$ with $H^1(\Gam;k\Gam)=0$ has one end.
Let $\Gam$ be a group and $J$ a subgroup with $H^1(\Gam;k[\Gam/J])=0$. Then $\Gam$ has no splitting over $J$.
If $n\ge3$, the group $\Gam$ is finitely presented and torsion-free, it has one end, $H^2(\Gam;\F_2\Gam)=0$, and $\Gam$ has no splitting over a finite or two-ended subgroup.

Let $P_*$ and $P'_*$ be complexes of left $\Z\Gam$-modules, free with given finite bases in degrees $0,1,2$, each with a surjection $P_0\to\Z$ such that $P_2\to P_1\to P_0\to\Z\to0$ is exact. Then $\bt{1}(P)=\bt{1}(P')$. If $P_*$ and $P'_*$ are bounded complexes of finitely generated free modules and are chain homotopy equivalent, then $\bt{p}(P)=\bt{p}(P')$ for all $p$.
The space $\Dsp$ is closed in $\lt(E;\R)$ and contains $\Dsp_0$, and $\bt{1}(\Gam)>0$ if and only if $\Dsp\ne\Dsp_0$.

Let $Q$ be a finite Poincar\'e complex of formal dimension $n$. Then $\bt{p}(\widetilde Q)=\bt{n-p}(\widetilde Q)$ for every integer $p$, where $\bt{p}=0$ for $p<0$. If $\Gam$ is infinite then $\bt{0}(\widetilde Q)=0$.

Let $\Gam$ be a $PD(n)$ group with $n\ge1$. Then $\Gam$ is torsion-free and infinite; $H^i(\Gam;V)\cong H_{n-i}(\Gam;V)$ for every $k\Gam$-module $V$ and every $i$, so that the conclusion of Lemma~\ref{lem:duality} holds for $\Gam$; and $\bt{p}(\Gam)=\bt{n-p}(\Gam)$ for every $p$, with $\bt{0}(\Gam)=0$.
